candidates.evidence: Four bands at 93.79, 161.27, 192.85 and 221.44 cm-1 (fit, sigma 0.06-0.7 cm-1). The top Computational Raman Database match is SSn = SnS, Pnma (mp-2231, crd:4496), score 0.88, with all four measured bands matched within 0-4 cm-1 after a 1.02 frequency scale. Its Ag/B3g/Ag/Ag labels match the experimental SnS modes in Fig. 2(c) of arXiv:2007.09362 (Sriv et al.), which show SnS bands near 95 (Ag), 160 (B3g), 192 (Ag) and 220 cm-1 (Ag) at 632.8 nm.

Not supported. The SnSe reference spectrum in Fig. 2(a) of arXiv:2007.09362 has its modes at roughly 30, 70, 110, 135 and 150 cm-1 (read by eye from the plot, about +/-5 cm-1) and essentially nothing between about 155 and 230 cm-1. Inside the measured 60-1100 cm-1 window, the SnSe modes near 70, 110 and 135-150 cm-1 are absent, while the measured 161, 193 and 221 cm-1 bands have no SnSe counterpart. The CRD SnSe entry did not rank in the top 5 matches.

hint_reasoning: The stated material is SnSe, but the spectrum does not match it. The four strong bands at 93.8, 161.3, 192.8 and 221.4 cm-1 are the orthorhombic SnS pattern (A_g/B_3g/A_g/A_g). Literature Raman spectra of SnSe (Pnma, same layered structure) have their main modes near 30, 70, 110 and 135-150 cm-1 and little above about 155 cm-1. The SnSe modes that fall inside the measured window (about 70, 110 and 135-150 cm-1) are missing, and the strongest measured band at 161-193 cm-1 has no SnSe partner. The sample is most likely SnS, not SnSe. Both are Pnma, so the identification relies on band positions, not on symmetry.

limits: The sample is not SnSe. The four measured bands match SnS, with the same orthorhombic Pnma structure. Identifying SnS versus SnSe rests only on band positions for one spectrum; I did not check a polarization series or resonance behaviour.

The measured window starts at 60.1 cm-1, so the lowest SnSe modes (about 30 cm-1, and about 35-40 cm-1 for a B3g mode) are outside it. Only the SnSe modes at about 70, 110 and 135-150 cm-1 can be tested, and they are absent.

No Si or other internal reference line is in the spectrum (si_line null), so the absolute calibration is unverified. Position errors are fit statistics only; I did not apply a calibration uncertainty. A shift of 1-2 cm-1 would not change the conclusion, since the SnSe-SnS difference is about 10-40 cm-1.

The reference band positions for SnS and SnSe come from Fig. 2 of arXiv:2007.09362 (632.8 nm excitation, not 532 nm, and not the same sample). SnSe values are read by eye from the figure (about +/-5 cm-1). I did not extract the numbers from a table, and I did not search the CRD specifically for SnSe.

The skill's reference library has no literature table or material note for SnS or SnSe (lookup_reference_modes returned an error for SnSe; list_relations has no SnSe or SnS relation). No relation was applied, so no layer number, strain, doping or defect density is reported.

The 221.4 cm-1 band is broad (FWHM 10.7 +/- 3.3 cm-1) and its position error is 0.7 cm-1, so it may be a shoulder or doublet. The fit plot does not show clear residual structure there, but it is less secure than the other three bands.
The fit is a single spectrum at 295 K with no polarization data and no substrate (none stated), so no polarization classification is given (the pattern fields are defaults, not measured).
